idiom_name: case class with val parameters + copy (scala.collection.immutable)
implementation_notes: Scala treats immutability as the default style: val creates an unassignable reference, a case class declares its constructor parameters as public vals with structural equality and a copy method, and scala.collection.immutable (List, Vector, Map, Set) is the ordinary collection package, where an update returns a new collection sharing the unchanged structure. The hand-written structure survives for performance-critical internals and for interop with Java APIs that expect JavaBean-style mutation. Arrays and java.util collections must be converted to immutable Scala types at the boundary, because they reintroduce mutation and reference equality.
pitfalls: case class copy is shallow: a List or Array component is shared with the copy, and a var declared in the class body is excluded from equals/hashCode while remaining mutable.
Array has reference equality even inside a case class, so an array component silently breaks value semantics and hashing; use Vector or List for value data.
Java collections and JavaBean setters arriving through interop reintroduce mutation; convert them to immutable Scala types at the boundary instead of passing them through.
